### R

```{r}
#| label: contour-line-3d-r
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of g(b, c) = b squared plus c squared for b and c from -3.5
#|   to 3.5. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin.
#|   Red circles of radius 1, 2 and 3 around the vertical axis, at heights
#|   1, 4 and 9, mark the contour lines. Two dots on the circle at height 4
#|   mark the points (2, 0) and (0, -2).
cl_b_sf <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 101)
cl_c_sf <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length.out = 101)
cl_grid_sf <- tidyr::expand_grid(b = cl_b_sf, c = cl_c_sf)
cl_value_sf <- cl_grid_sf$b^2 + cl_grid_sf$c^2
cl_n_sf <- length(cl_c_sf)
cl_z_sf <- matrix(cl_value_sf, nrow = cl_n_sf)
cl_angle_sf <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 101)
cl_heights_sf <- c(1, 4, 9)
cl_rings_sf <- tidyr::expand_grid(k = cl_heights_sf, angle = cl_angle_sf)
cl_rings_sf$radius <- sqrt(cl_rings_sf$k)
cl_rings_sf$b <- cl_rings_sf$radius * cos(cl_rings_sf$angle)
cl_rings_sf$c <- cl_rings_sf$radius * sin(cl_rings_sf$angle)
cl_marks_b_sf <- c(2, 0)
cl_marks_c_sf <- c(0, -2)
cl_marks_z_sf <- c(4, 4)
cl_marks_sf <- tibble::tibble(
  b = cl_marks_b_sf,
  c = cl_marks_c_sf,
  z = cl_marks_z_sf
)
cl_ring_line_sf <- list(color = "#D55E00", width = 5)
cl_marker_sf <- list(color = "black", size = 5)
cl_stops_sf <- c(0, 1)
cl_cols_sf <- c("#CCE0F0", "#0072B2")
cl_scale_sf <- list(cl_stops_sf, cl_cols_sf)
cl_eye_sf <- list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9)
cl_camera_sf <- list(eye = cl_eye_sf)
cl_xaxis_sf <- list(title = "b")
cl_yaxis_sf <- list(title = "c")
cl_zaxis_sf <- list(title = "g(b, c)")
cl_scene_sf <- list(
  xaxis = cl_xaxis_sf,
  yaxis = cl_yaxis_sf,
  zaxis = cl_zaxis_sf,
  camera = cl_camera_sf
)
plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_surface(
    x = cl_b_sf,
    y = cl_c_sf,
    z = cl_z_sf,
    colorscale = cl_scale_sf,
    showscale = FALSE,
    opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  plotly::add_trace(
    data = cl_rings_sf,
    x = ~b,
    y = ~c,
    z = ~k,
    split = ~k,
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "lines",
    line = cl_ring_line_sf,
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  plotly::add_markers(
    data = cl_marks_sf,
    x = ~b,
    y = ~c,
    z = ~z,
    showlegend = FALSE,
    marker = cl_marker_sf
  ) |>
  plotly::layout(scene = cl_scene_sf)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: contour-line-3d-python
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| results: asis
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of g(b, c) = b squared plus c squared for b and c from -3.5
#|   to 3.5. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin.
#|   Red circles of radius 1, 2 and 3 around the vertical axis, at heights
#|   1, 4 and 9, mark the contour lines. Two dots on the circle at height 4
#|   mark the points (2, 0) and (0, -2).
import html
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig_alt = (
    "Surface plot of g(b, c) = b squared plus c squared for b and c from -3.5 "
    "to 3.5. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin. Red "
    "circles of radius 1, 2 and 3 around the vertical axis, at heights 1, 4 and "
    "9, mark the contour lines. Two dots on the circle at height 4 mark the "
    "points (2, 0) and (0, -2)."
)

cl_s_3d = np.linspace(-3.5, 3.5, 101)
cl_b_3d, cl_c_3d = np.meshgrid(cl_s_3d, cl_s_3d)
cl_g_3d = cl_b_3d**2 + cl_c_3d**2
cl_angle_3d = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 101)
fig = go.Figure(data=[
    go.Surface(
        x=cl_s_3d,
        y=cl_s_3d,
        z=cl_g_3d,
        colorscale=[[0, "#CCE0F0"], [1, "#0072B2"]],
        showscale=False,
        opacity=0.6,
        showlegend=False,
    ),
])
for k in [1, 4, 9]:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d(
        x=np.sqrt(k) * np.cos(cl_angle_3d),
        y=np.sqrt(k) * np.sin(cl_angle_3d),
        z=np.full_like(cl_angle_3d, k), mode="lines",
        line=dict(color="#D55E00", width=5), showlegend=False));
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d(
    x=[2, 0], y=[0, -2], z=[4, 4], mode="markers",
    marker=dict(color="black", size=4), showlegend=False));
fig.update_layout(
    scene=dict(
        xaxis_title="b",
        yaxis_title="c",
        zaxis_title="g(b, c)",
        camera=dict(eye=dict(x=1.6, y=-1.6, z=0.9)),
    ),
    showlegend=False,
);
print(
    "```{=html}\n"
    + f'<div role="img" aria-label="{html.escape(fig_alt)}">\n'
    + fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn")
    + "\n</div>\n```"
)
```

```{python}
#| label: contour-line-3d-python-static
#| echo: !expr isFALSE(knitr::is_html_output())
#| eval: !expr isFALSE(knitr::is_html_output())
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of g(b, c) = b squared plus c squared for b and c from -3.5
#|   to 3.5. The surface is a bowl with its lowest point at the origin.
#|   Red circles of radius 1, 2 and 3 around the vertical axis, at heights
#|   1, 4 and 9, mark the contour lines. Two dots on the circle at height 4
#|   mark the points (2, 0) and (0, -2).
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

cl_b_3d, cl_c_3d = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-3.5, 3.5, 101),
                               np.linspace(-3.5, 3.5, 101))
cl_g_3d = cl_b_3d**2 + cl_c_3d**2
cl_angle_3d = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 101)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
ax.plot_surface(cl_b_3d, cl_c_3d, cl_g_3d, color="#0072B2", alpha=0.6)
for k in [1, 4, 9]:
    ax.plot(np.sqrt(k) * np.cos(cl_angle_3d),
            np.sqrt(k) * np.sin(cl_angle_3d),
            k, color="#D55E00", linewidth=2)
ax.scatter([2, 0], [0, -2], [4, 4], color="black")
ax.set_xlabel("b")
ax.set_ylabel("c")
ax.set_zlabel("g(b, c)")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) of $g(b, c) = b^2 + c^2$, the surface whose [contour lines](#def-contour-line) are in @fig-contour-line.
The red circles are the contour lines at heights $1$, $4$ and $9$,
and the dots are the points $(2, 0)$ and $(0, -2)$ of @exm-contour-line on the one at height $4$.

:::
